title: Option Elimination Strategies
tagline: Year 4 — Killing options with the last digit, parity, divisibility, size bounds and sign before doing the full calculation

introduction.overview: In a multiple-choice test you do not always have to compute the answer; you have to identify which option it is. Elimination uses properties that every correct answer must have: the right last digit, parity, divisibility, size between bounds, or sign. Each property can be checked in seconds and often leaves a single option. Elimination is also a safe fallback when time runs out, since each removed option raises the chance of a correct guess.
introduction.placementRelevance: Online tests are multiple-choice and timed; elimination saves time on arithmetic-heavy items.
introduction.realWorldContext: Plausibility checks catch errors in any calculation.

learningObjectives: Use the last digit and parity to eliminate
Use divisibility tests and digital roots
Use sign and direction of change

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: The last digit of a product depends only on the last digits of the factors. A square cannot end in 2, 3, 7 or 8.

coreDefinitions: Elimination: removing options that cannot be correct.
Bound: a lower or upper limit for the answer.
Parity: whether a number is odd or even.
Digital root: a check on the digits.
Plausibility: whether the answer has the right size.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The right answer has to satisfy simple tests that wrong options often fail.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Before computing, ask: what must the last digit be? the parity? the rough size? Then remove options.

mainNarrative: 47 × 53: the last digit is 7 × 3 = 21, so 1. Options ending in 2 or 6 are out; the size is near 50² = 2,500, so 2,591 is also out.
156 + 289: even + odd is odd, so even options are out.
The average of 12, 18 and 30 must lie between 12 and 30; options 10 and 60 are out.
x² = 1,369: x lies between 35 and 40 (since 35² = 1,225 and 40² = 1,600) and ends in 3 or 7, giving 37.
For a remainder on division by 3, the answer must be 0, 1 or 2, so an option "3" is out.

deepDiveAspects.title: Elimination is not guessing
deepDiveAspects.content: Each removed option raises the probability of a correct choice from 25% to 33%, 50% and so on.

deepDiveAspects.title: Order of tests
deepDiveAspects.content: Do the fastest test first: last digit, then parity, then size.

solvedExamples.title: Last digit
solvedExamples.question: 47 × 53 has options 2,481; 2,492; 2,501; 2,591. Which can you reject at once?

solvedExamples.title: Range
solvedExamples.question: The average of 12, 18 and 30 can be 10, 20 or 60. Which is possible?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Test last digit, parity and rough size; compute only if two options survive.

placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Build a habit: last digit, parity, size.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Question setters design traps that pass a single test.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I eliminate by last digit?
Can I decide when to compute?
